newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Cullen calls for parliamentary debate on NZ dlr.
newsitem.headline: Cullen calls for parliamentary debate on NZ dlr.

text.p: Labour finance spokesman Michael Cullen on Wednesday called on the government to reconvene Parliament early to discuss "the economic situation and the exchange rate crisis".

Parliament is not scheduled to meet until February 18 but Cullen said that it was time Treasurer and Acting Prime Minister Winston Peters lived up to at least one of his pre-election promises by taking Parliament and democracy more seriously.
"MPs should not be waiting around until February 18 to get to grips with the exchange rate crisis," Cullen said.
He said Parliament could be called back as soon as next Tuesday.

Prime Minister Jim Bolger on Tuesday maintained the government's hands-off stance on the issue of New Zealand's currency, saying the markets set the dollar's value and its level was a reflection of overseas investors' faith in the New Zealand economy.
Peters campaigned hard on the exchange rate before the election, saying it was crippling exporters.
But as it has continued to rise since, he has said nothing.
"Parliament must place this marshmallow puff Treasurer under scrutiny," Cullen said.
"We need a clear debate immediately on the Government's spending programme and how this relates to its intentions for the economy.
"We need Mr Bolger to explain how a large current account deficit combined with an over-valued dollar is a sign of the strength of the New Zealand economy.

"We deserve to have Mr Peters explain why he raved against New Zealand's so-called monetarist experiment for years and now is happy to relegate himself to the role of Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash's lab assistant."
Peters is acting prime minister while Bolger is in Antarctica for four days.
